skill.name: schedules
skill.description: Schedule SpecStream list refreshes from hourly to yearly with spending limits per run and per month. Send new and changed records to an approved destination.
skill.summary: Refresh SpecStream lists on a schedule and review changes within agreed spending limits.
skill.author: specstream

security_audit.summary: The backtick alerts are Markdown, the URL points to the configured SpecStream service, and the reconnaissance alerts do not describe host inspection. The skill requires approval to create schedules but does not require approval of recipients or event scope before configuring outbound delivery. No evidence of prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Outbound delivery setup lacks an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before configuring delivery, show the exact destination and the records or account events it will receive. Require approval from an authorized user and verify the destination against workspace policy.

content.value_statement: Manual refreshes make it hard to track which web records changed and how much updates cost. Schedule SpecStream refreshes with spending limits and send new or changed records to an approved destination.
actual_capabilities: Interpret a refresh request and quote its scope before creating a schedule.
Set a cadence, first run, end date, per-run limit, and monthly spending limit.
Route new and changed records to SpecStream notifications, Slack, a connected tool, or an HTTPS webhook.
List running or paused schedules and inspect completed, blocked, and missed runs.
Show before and after values for changed facts with the page that supports the new value.
Pause, resume, or delete a schedule with its current version when the owner asks.
limitations: The skill requires a configured SpecStream MCP server.
Fixed intervals must be at least one hour. Monthly limits follow the UTC calendar month.
Creating a schedule does not fund it. Blocked or missed runs are not automatically purchased later.
Slack and webhook delivery require an eligible plan. Slack delivery is limited to the connected workspace.

use_cases.title: Track Supplier Catalog Changes
use_cases.description: Refresh a supplier list weekly and review changed prices or availability with links to the source pages.

use_cases.title: Review Scheduled Run Costs
use_cases.description: Compare monthly schedule totals with agreed limits and check why a run was blocked or missed.

use_cases.title: Send Record Changes to an Internal System
use_cases.description: Route new and changed records to an approved HTTPS webhook and verify signatures before processing them.

prompt_templates.title: List Existing Schedules
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review schedules without making changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: List my SpecStream schedules. Show which are running or paused and list each schedule's per-run and monthly spending limits.

prompt_templates.title: Quote a Weekly Refresh
prompt_templates.scenario: Estimate the cost before creating a recurring refresh.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how SpecStream interprets a weekly refresh of my supplier list and quote the scope. Ask me for the start date, end date, and spending limits before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Schedule After Approval
prompt_templates.scenario: Set up a recurring refresh with agreed spending limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a weekly refresh for my supplier list, from January 4 through March 29, 2027. Propose limits of $5 per run and $20 per UTC month. Wait for my approval, then create the schedule and show both monthly totals.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Signed Webhook Delivery
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: send changes from an existing schedule to an internal receiver.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check webhook eligibility and get the current version of my supplier schedule. Show the exact HTTPS destination and the record scope, then wait for my approval before configuring delivery. Explain how the receiver should verify signatures and discard duplicates without printing the signing secret.

output_examples.input: Summarize the last three refreshes for my supplier list.
output: Monday: Completed. One supplier changed a listed price.
Tuesday: Blocked. The run would exceed the agreed monthly limit.
Wednesday: Missed. No refresh result was recorded.

output_examples.input: Show what changed for Northstar Supplies in the last completed refresh.
output_examples.output: The listed price rose from $18 to $20. The change record links to the supplier page where SpecStream observed the new price.

best_practices: Review the interpreted scope, quote, timing, and spending limits with the user before creating a schedule.
Confirm the recipient and event scope with an authorized user before enabling delivery.
Store webhook signing secrets securely. Verify the signature and timestamp, and use the event ID to discard duplicates.
anti_patterns: Treating an account balance as permission to exceed the agreed spending limits.
Reporting blocked or missed runs as successful refreshes with no changes.
Trusting webhook records before checking their signature and timestamp.

faq.question: How often can a list refresh?
faq.answer: Fixed intervals start at one hour. A calendar schedule supports calendar-based timing, up to yearly refreshes.

faq.question: Does creating a schedule pay for future runs?
faq.answer: No. Creating a schedule does not fund it. Confirm the per-run limit and the UTC monthly limit before creating it.

faq.question: Does setting a delivery destination start a refresh?
faq.answer: No. Setting delivery chooses where future new and changed records go. It does not run the schedule.

faq.question: Where can new or changed records go?
faq.answer: SpecStream can send them to its notifications, a channel in the connected Slack workspace, a connected tool, or an HTTPS webhook.

faq.question: When is the webhook signing secret shown?
faq.answer: SpecStream returns the secret once when webhook delivery is configured. Store it securely and do not paste it into code or chat.

faq.question: Can I change or remove a running schedule?
faq.answer: The owner can request a pause, resume, or deletion. The update requires the schedule's current version.
